(2) Chantal Kapani, LeadDev, 'The tokenmaxxing hype didn't last long', 17 Aug 2026, https://leaddev.com/reporting/the-tokenmaxxing-hype-didnt-last-long. (3) Sarah Perez, TechCrunch, 'Meta's Adam Mosseri says AI token budgets could soon be capped per engineer', 14 Jul 2026, https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/14/metas-adam-mosseri-says-ai-token-budgets-could-soon-be-capped-per-engineer/. (4) Bedard, Kropp, Hsu, Karaman, Hawes, Rosen Kellerman, HBR, 'When Using AI Leads to Brain Fry', 5 Mar 2026, https://hbr.org/2026/03/when-using-ai-leads-to-brain-fry
source_tier: Press (heise relaying The Information; TechCrunch); practitioner media reporting a survey (LeadDev); HBR article for the originating claim.
access_status: Heise, LeadDev article and TechCrunch opened and read via fetch. HBR page: only the truncated summary was visible (paywalled); the Meta lines-of-code sentence was NOT found. Original The Information and Business Insider pieces NOT opened (Business Insider/HR Grapevine returned 403 or were not found). LeadDev AI Impact Report 2026 full report NOT opened; it is gated or pre-registration only (not confirmed which).
sponsor_and_incentive: LeadDev sells engineering-leadership content and events and runs the survey; HBR authors are BCG-affiliated consultants. Heise/TechCrunch/The Information are independent press. Meta HR has an interest in framing Checkpoint as an 'impact' tool.
exact_quotes: Heise (4 Feb 2026): Checkpoint is 'the name of the AI-powered performance tracking tool'; Meta HR manager: not 'a dedicated activity tracker, but rather an instrument for capturing effectiveness'; tool reportedly tallies lines of code 'coded with the help of AI' (English version of German original; German wording not seen). | LeadDev (17 Aug 2026): '58% of respondents say their organization currently measures AI impact via token usage'; '57% say it's ineffective at gauging real value'; 'only 19% of respondents call tokenmaxxing effective'; Meta shut down its internal token leaderboard 'Claudeonomics' over concerns that it 'rewarded token consumption rather than meaningful impact'. | TechCrunch (14 Jul 2026): Mosseri: 'Meta doesn't currently have token caps for any employee'; 'It's not that hard to build a token incinerator, and that doesn't create a lot of value'; Meta 'shut down an internal AI token spend leaderboard'. | HBR (5 Mar 2026) summary visible: 'As firms increasingly incentivize employees to build and oversee complex teams of agents—for example, by measuring and rewarding token consumption as a proxy for performance—people are...'
date_and_recency: Heise 4 Feb 2026; HBR 5 Mar 2026; TechCrunch 14 Jul 2026; LeadDev 17 Aug 2026 (report described as 'upcoming'). Survey collection window not stated in opened pages.
key_claims: Meta's Checkpoint tool reportedly counts lines of code written with AI help as one input to performance assessment, alongside about 200 other data points (per The Information via heise). HBR summary says firms measure and reward token consumption as a proxy for performance. Meta ran an internal token leaderboard (Claudeonomics) and shut it down; Mosseri says token incinerators create little value. LeadDev says its survey found most organisations measure AI impact by token usage and most of those find it ineffective.
headline_figures: LeadDev article: 58% say their organisation measures AI impact via token usage; 57% say that is ineffective at gauging real value; 19% call tokenmaxxing effective (AI Impact Report 2026, upcoming, Aug 2026). NOTE: the 58% is the share who MEASURE by tokens, not the share who call it ineffective; the task premise ('58% say ineffective') is wrong per the opened article. 'About 200 other data points' for Checkpoint (heise via The Information; figure came from the search summary of reports, heise page text opened only confirmed Checkpoint and lines-of-code tally) [uncertain]. Survey size of 591 engineering leaders appeared only in a search summary, not an opened page [uncertain].
sample_unit_and_population: LeadDev: respondents are engineering leaders/organisations (sample size not stated in the opened article; 591 unverified) [uncertain]. Checkpoint concerns Meta software engineers. Not a study of individual cognitive load.
observed_vs_stated: LeadDev figures are self-reported survey answers. Meta Checkpoint account is anonymous-source press reporting of an internal tool; Meta's leaderboard shutdown is reported by TechCrunch/LeadDev.
what_makes_oversight_tiring: Not addressed by these sources. HBR summary only links incentives to build and oversee complex teams of agents with people feeling strain (text truncated).
consequence_for_quality: Sources say token-count metrics reward consumption rather than impact (LeadDev on Meta's leaderboard) and that token incinerators create little value (Mosseri). No quality or error data on lines-of-code metric opened.
what_reduces_the_load: Meta shut down the leaderboard and Mosseri says it cut silly things; per-engineer budgets are discussed but would need to reflect trust the engineer uses them ROI-positively. Meta HR frames Checkpoint as impact evidence, not activity tracking.
limitations_stated: Heise relies on internal sources via The Information. LeadDev article calls the report 'upcoming'; full report gating not confirmed. TechCrunch article describes no formal performance system.
counter_evidence: Meta HR says Checkpoint is not an activity tracker. Mosseri says Meta has no token caps for any employee. A search summary (not opened) claims Meta used lines of code as a rating input only as one of many signals.
verification_status: VERIFIED against opened sources: Checkpoint exists and reportedly tallies AI-assisted lines of code (heise, secondhand via The Information); LeadDev 58% measure / 57% ineffective / 19% effective; Meta shut down token leaderboard (LeadDev, TechCrunch); HBR summary on token consumption as proxy (summary text only). NOT verified: HBR sentence that Meta 'includes the number of lines of code generated by AI as a performance metric' [uncertain]; Business Insider and The Information originals [uncertain]; the 300% or 200% bonus multiplier [uncertain]; LeadDev '58% ineffective' framing is contradicted by the article.
usable_claim: The Information reported (via heise, Feb 2026) that Meta's Checkpoint tool counts lines of code written with AI help as one input among many in performance assessment; Meta HR said it is not an activity tracker. HBR (Mar 2026) says some firms measure and reward token consumption as a performance proxy. LeadDev reports 58% of surveyed organisations measure AI impact by token usage and 57% say that is ineffective at gauging real value. Meta shut down its token leaderboard (TechCrunch, LeadDev).
do_not_use: '58% say token metrics are ineffective' (it is 57%; 58% is the share that measure). Any statement that Meta requires or rates engineers on AI line counts as a sole metric. HBR attribution of the Meta lines-of-code claim (not found in opened text). Bonus multiplier figures, 591 sample size, 73.7 trillion token figures (unopened sources).
overlap_with_existing_essays: Not checked against the trust essay, Verification Gap or Checking Isn't Catching; none of these sources were compared to them.
